summary: Native renderer, stage and streaming server are created before the try/finally, and the WebRTC signalling port is hard-coded to 49100 independent of --port.
failure_scenario: Start a second observer with a different --port (or leave 49100 held by another process): the HTTP server binds, ovstage.Stage, ovrtx.Renderer and ovstream.initialize() succeed, then server.start(... webrtc_signal_port=49100) raises. The exception escapes before line 125 try, so server.close, ovstream.shutdown, renderer.destroy and stage.destroy never run and the process exits with live native objects, while the module itself notes wrapper destructors can block. The same applies to a failure in wrapper() for the waiting scene (line 68). The browser also hard-codes 49100 (viewer/app.js:123), so --port cannot separate two observers, and a second RTX owner is created before the failure.
evidence: Read observe.py lines 52-125 and viewer/app.js:120-125: only the HTTP port is configurable; every native allocation sits between the GpuPacer() call and the try at line 125. Not executed (no GPU/ovstream); teardown behavior of a leaked native Renderer at interpreter exit is unverified.

summary: GpuPacer ordering: observe, render_motion.render, rtx.open_renderer, smoke.render, simulate and video_io.encode_mp4 construct GpuPacer (stop check, affinity, priority) before importing/initializing ovrtx, ovstage, ovphysx, nvimgcodec or PyNvVideoCodec. tools/check_gpu_work.py run with python -I passes (CPU-only mock of duty, stop during idle, startup stop, mask idempotence).

Stop and teardown paths: simulate.py destroys PhysX and the stage in nested finally blocks and detaches only when attached; rtx.open_renderer and loaded_scene destroy in finally; KeyboardInterrupt from gpu.batch exit discards the finished frame but unwinds cleanly. observe.py with a pending native operation exits via os._exit(2) by documented design.

engine.py child worker: subprocess runs simulate.py under -I with explicit sys.path insert, so it builds its own GpuPacer; a stop in the child surfaces as a nonzero exit and RuntimeError in the parent, so stop is not swallowed. Child inherits the parent's affinity.

publish.py/physics_usd.pack: the package is written to a temporary _<hex>.usdz and renamed, and current.json is replaced atomically; the observer ignores non-numeric stems, so it never lists or loads a half-written revision.

observe.py candidate flow: failed wrapper, open_usd or frame errors reject the revision and restore the previous stage; attach/detach failures go fatal; disconnect with a pending candidate pauses rendering and resumes on reconnect; reconnect clears held. No stale-queue or double-destroy path found by reading.
video_io encode: the .partial.mp4 is removed on any BaseException (including stop) and the muxer is released first; NVENC/decode/NV12 work runs inside gpu.batch except encoder/muxer creation.

field_view.py runs finite Warp/CUDA work without GpuPacer, but so do texture_compute and mesh_compute (finite tasks); not reported as a defect. observe.wrapper() runs viewer_scene.py with no timeout on the main loop (CPU only); a hang there is hypothetical and not reported. setup_viewer.py verifies the sha512 before writing and extracts only fixed member names.
Not executed: any GPU, ovrtx, ovstage, ovphysx, ovstream, nvimgcodec, NVENC or Windows affinity/priority call. All findings and checks are from source reading plus the CPU-only check_gpu_work.py run.
